sourceEvidence.claim: Chlamydiae life cycle and diseases (cannot make their own ATP; obligate intracellular; the ▘-bulleted EB/RB forms with the printed enfectious gloss; C. trachomatis conjunctivitis with inline photo marker A; C. pneumoniae and C. psittaci atypical pneumonia by aerosol)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Chlamydiae cannot make their own ATP. They
are obligate intracellular organisms that cause
mucosal infections. 2 forms:
▘ Elementary body (small, dense)
is “enfectious” and enters cell via
endocytosis; transforms into reticulate body.
▘ Reticulate body replicates in cell by fission;
reorganizes into elementary bodies.
Chlamydia trachomatis causes neonatal
and follicular adult conjunctivitis A ,
nongonococcal urethritis, PID, and reactive
arthritis.
Chlamydophila pneumoniae and Chlamydophila
psittaci cause atypical pneumonia; transmitted
by aerosol.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Chlamydial cell wall + lab + treatment (lacks classic peptidoglycan — reduced muramic acid — β-lactams ineffective; the printed Chlamys=cloak gloss; psittaci's avian reservoir; PCR/NAAT; cytoplasmic inclusions on Giemsa or fluorescent antibody stain; doxycycline, azithromycin for pregnancy, + ceftriaxone if concurrent gonorrhea positive)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Chlamydial cell wall lacks classic peptidoglycan
(due to reduced muramic acid), rendering
β-lactam antibiotics ineffective.
Chlamys = cloak (intracellular).
C psittaci—has an avian reservoir (parrots),
causes atypical pneumonia.
Lab diagnosis: PCR, NAAT. Cytoplasmic
inclusions (reticulate bodies) seen on Giemsa
or fluorescent antibody–stained smear.
Treatment: doxycycline, azithromycin (for
pregnant patients). Add ceftriaxone if
concurrent gonorrhea testing is positive.

sourceEvidence.claim: Gardnerella vaginalis entry (pleomorphic gram-variable rod; bacterial vaginosis; gray fishy nonpainful discharge vs vaginitis; not sexually transmitted; anaerobic overgrowth with ↓ lactobacilli; clue cells with the inline arrow-in-A photo marker)
sourceEvidence.quote:
A pleomorphic, gram-variable rod involved in
bacterial vaginosis. Presents as a gray vaginal
discharge with a fishy smell; nonpainful (vs
vaginitis). Associated with sexual activity,
but not sexually transmitted. Bacterial
vaginosis is also characterized by overgrowth
of certain anaerobic bacteria in vagina (due
to ↓ lactobacilli). Clue cells (vaginal epithelial
cells covered with Gardnerella) have stippled
appearance along outer margin (arrow in A ).

sourceEvidence.claim: Rocky Mountain spotted fever block (R. rickettsii, tick vector; South Atlantic states especially North Carolina; the rash starts at wrists A — inline photo marker — and ankles then spreads to trunk, palms, soles; the classic triad headache-fever-rash vasculitis; the printed CARS mnemonic; the printed wrists/trunk mnemonic)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Rocky Mountain
spotted fever

Rickettsia rickettsii, vector is tick. Despite its
name, disease occurs primarily in the South
Atlantic states, especially North Carolina.
Rash typically starts at wrists A and ankles and
then spreads to trunk, palms, and soles.

Classic triad—headache, fever, rash (vasculitis).
Palms and soles rash is seen in Coxsackievirus
A infection (hand, foot, and mouth disease),
Rocky Mountain spotted fever, and 2° Syphilis
(you drive CARS using your palms and soles).
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Mycoplasma clinical block (atypical walking pneumonia with curly quotes; <30 years old; outbreaks in military recruits, prisons, colleges; macrolides, doxycycline, or fluoroquinolone — penicillin ineffective since Mycoplasma has no cell wall)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Classic cause of atypical “walking pneumonia”
(insidious onset, headache, nonproductive
cough, patchy or diffuse interstitial infiltrate,
macular rash).
Occurs frequently in those <30 years old;
outbreaks in military recruits, prisons, colleges.
Treatment: macrolides, doxycycline, or
fluoroquinolone (penicillin ineffective since
Mycoplasma has no cell wall).

sourceEvidence.claim: Mycoplasma lab block (not seen on Gram stain; Pleomorphic with inline photo marker A; membrane sterols; Eaton agar; CXR more severe than presentation; cold agglutinins IgM agglutinating RBCs; the printed cold-without-a-coat mnemonic)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Not seen on Gram stain. Pleomorphic A .
Bacterial membrane contains sterols for
stability. Grown on Eaton agar.
CXR appears more severe than patient
presentation. High titer of cold agglutinins (IgM),
which can agglutinate RBCs. Mycoplasma gets
cold without a coat (no cell wall).

kypExtensions.summary: The EB/RB cycle read through the wall rule (no peptidoglycan → β-lactams fail → doxycycline/azithromycin axis) with the serotype tri-split (A-C blindness, D-K the 1-2-week neonatal conjunctivitis vs the gonococcal 2-5-day pair of M12, L1-L3 the buboes); the zoonotic directory read as a transmission map (the tick boards, the louse, the fleas, the aerosol exceptions); the rash geometry (RMSF wrists-to-palms vasculitis vs typhus central-sparing) with the morulae cell-lineage axis and Q fever's no-rash-no-vector culture-negative endocarditis; Mycoplasma's no-wall set (cold agglutinins, CXR worse than the patient, not on Gram stain) paired with chlamydiae's no-peptidoglycan as the same therapy logic; and Gardnerella's vaginosis-vs-vaginitis split (nonpainful, pH, whiff, clue cells) — labeled as integrations.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the sections without the cross-chapter wiring or the synthesis; these integrations are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + both mechanism captions + callout + patterns + traps + mnemonics + miniCase
